issue_context.title: Threshold helper doesn't allow float for upper/lower
issue_context.body:
### The problem

When creating a threshold helper in the UI I can only use an integer value for upper and lower. However [the doc](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/threshold/#lower) for these fields says it should allow a float. And in YAML it does allow a float. It should do the same in the UI.
![Screen Shot 2022-07-21 at 11 40 36 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2037026/180256857-09778e49-0126-48fc-99d0-73636903ca30.png)

UPDATE: Same behavior with hysteresis:
![Screen Shot 2022-07-21 at 11 53 33 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2037026/180258691-981d5c7e-3589-4051-86b0-dc787fd4fc66.png)

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2022.7.6

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

threshold

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/threshold

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
binary_sensor:
- platform: threshold
  entity_id: sensor.devices_with_low_battery
  name: Devices with low battery
  device_class: battery
  upper: 0.5
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

There is a second issue with this helper: I created a threshold sensor with only a lower value. When I tried to change it with the helper I got an error saying an upper value was required, which it is not. Now I can't get the threshold sensor to work at all, it only shows "Unknown"

I was able to create the threshold with a float (on the web UI). 
However, when editing (on the iOS app) I am having two of the issues mentioned here:
* Only able to enter integer values
* Both upper and lower bounds are required, even if the helper was created with only one.

Hm I can't actually edit my UI threshold sensors anymore, I just see this:
![Screenshot_20220729-105213](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2037026/181786649-c6130103-5101-4358-924e-c594a7f91d80.png)

I was trying to figure out why I didn't get a notification when my sensor broke the threshold. I might have to move all these back to yaml...

Workaround for not being able to save single-bound thresholds: 
1. Update all the fields you want to update
2. Put any value in the field you don't need
3. Save
4. Remove the value in the field you don't need
5. Save

I have noticed that in the web UI the field turns red when the text box contains a float, but will still let you save. I assume this is either because the wrong field type is being used, or it is an issue with the number box itself.
